content.title: About
content.content: Breakfast Tart, Lowfat is a light pastry made from whole‑grain flour, fat‑free cottage cheese and egg whites. It contains minimal saturated fat while remaining flavorful and nutritious, making it ideal for a morning meal.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The tart is prepared without butter, cutting the calorie count by almost half compared with traditional versions.
Fat‑free cottage cheese provides a good source of calcium and protein.
It is often served with berry sauce or fresh fruit, boosting vitamin and antioxidant content.
Egg whites give the tart structure without adding extra fat.

items.title: Low Fat Content
items.content: The tart contains less than 5 g of fat per 100 g, suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Rich in Protein
items.content: Cottage cheese and egg whites supply about 12 g of protein per serving, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: Calcium Source
items.content: Provides calcium important for bone and teeth health.

items.title: Low Glycemic Index
items.content: Whole‑grain flour slows carbohydrate absorption, helping maintain stable blood sugar levels.

items.title: B‑Vitamin Rich
items.content: Egg whites and whole‑grain flour contain B2, B6 and folate, essential for energy metabolism.

items.title: Egg Allergy
items.content: The tart contains egg whites, which may trigger allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Lactose Content
items.content: Fat‑free cottage cheese may contain trace lactose; those with intolerance should choose a lactose‑free alternative.

items.title: Sodium
items.content: Some recipes add a small amount of salt; limit intake if you need to control sodium.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy the tart warm or cold, sliced into portions. Serve with low‑fat yogurt, berry sauce, or fresh fruit. For a more filling breakfast, add a side of nuts or seeds.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the tart in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. For longer storage, freeze it in a separate bag – it retains flavor and texture for up to 2 months. Reheat in the oven 5‑10 minutes at 180 °C before serving.

content.title: About
content.content: Ceviche is a dish of fresh fish or seafood cured in lime or lemon juice, mixed with onion, chili pepper, and fresh herbs. The acidity “cooks” the fish, giving it a tender, aromatic texture. It is traditionally popular in Latin American countries, especially Peru and Mexico.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Ceviche is considered Peru’s national dish and is recognized as part of the country’s cultural heritage.
The acidic marinade not only adds flavor but also destroys most pathogenic bacteria.
There are many regional variations: Mexico adds tomatoes, Chile uses cilantro, and Peru includes sweet potato and corn crisps.
Ceviche is traditionally served with corn cakes (choclo) or sweet potatoes to balance the acidity.
The earliest recorded ceviche recipe dates back to the 17th century, when Spanish colonists adapted local fish‑curing methods.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Ceviche provides complete protein from fish, essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Omega‑3 fatty acids
items.content: Fatty fish used in ceviche are rich in omega‑3s, supporting heart health and reducing inflammation.

items.title: Low‑calorie dish
items.content: Thanks to the citrus‑based marinade, ceviche is relatively low in calories, making it suitable for weight‑management diets.

items.title: Vitamins and minerals
items.content: The dish supplies vitamin C (from lime), vitamin A, potassium, and iron, which aid immunity and metabolism.

items.title: Probiotic effect
items.content: The acidic environment encourages beneficial bacteria, promoting a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: Risk of foodborne illness
items.content: If the fish is not fresh or the marinade is insufficiently acidic, there is a risk of salmonella or listeria infection.

items.title: Seafood allergy
items.content: People allergic to fish or shellfish may experience severe reactions to ceviche.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: When soy sauce or added salt is used, the dish can become high in sodium, which is undesirable for hypertension.

items.title: Acid reflux
items.content: The lime juice may exacerbate heartburn in sensitive individuals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve ceviche chilled in small portions, often with corn cakes, sweet potatoes, or avocado. Garnish with fresh cilantro, cherry tomatoes, and extra lime juice to taste.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep prepared ceviche in the refrigerator for no more than 24 hours, as the acidic cure loses effectiveness over time. Store in an airtight container; discard if the fish changes color or develops an off‑odor.

cream-puff-no-filling-or-icing.title: Cream Puff without Filling or Icing

content.title: About
content.content: A cream puff without filling or icing is a light, airy pastry made from water, butter, flour, and eggs, baked until golden. In this version the puff is served plain, without sweet filling or glaze, making it a neutral base for various toppings or simply a light snack.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The classic éclair originates from French cuisine and was originally called “cream pastry”.
The dough used for éclairs is called choux pastry: water and butter are boiled, flour is added and cooked briefly before eggs are incorporated.
Plain éclairs are often used in culinary schools to practice shaping and baking choux dough.
Éclairs can be made sweet or savory depending on the ingredients added to the dough and the final serving.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: The puff provides carbohydrates from flour that quickly supply the body with energy.

items.title: Low sugar content
items.content: Without glaze or filling the product is less sweet, suitable for those monitoring sugar intake.

items.title: Contains quality protein
items.content: Eggs in the dough deliver high‑quality protein needed for tissue repair.

items.title: Provides plant‑based fats
items.content: Butter used in the dough supplies monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fatty acids.

items.title: Versatile base
items.content: Neutral flavor allows pairing with nutritious fillings such as cottage cheese, vegetable purées, or nut butters.

items.title: Egg or gluten allergy
items.content: The dough contains eggs and wheat flour, which may trigger allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: High calorie density
items.content: Despite lacking sugar, the puff remains calorie‑dense due to butter and carbs; portion control is advised.

items.title: Possible trans fats with improper fat choice
items.content: Using margarine instead of a quality butter can introduce trans fats, which are detrimental to heart health.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Plain cream puffs can be enjoyed as a light snack, split open and filled with cottage cheese, berry purée, savory vegetable ragout, or lean meat filling. They also serve as a base for dessert plates, topped with fresh fruit and sauces.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store baked puffs in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2 days. For longer keeping, refrigerate up to 5 days or freeze for up to 2 months. Reheat in the oven for 5‑7 minutes before serving to restore crispness.

egg-sandwich-on-white-bread-with-meat-an.title: Egg sandwich on white bread with meat and cheese

content.title: About
content.content: An egg sandwich with meat and cheese on white bread is a classic breakfast or light lunch. It consists of two slices of soft white bread, a fried egg, a slice of cooked or smoked meat (such as ham or bacon), and a meltable cheese that softens from the heat.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Egg sandwiches have been popular in the US and UK for over a century.
White bread is often used for its soft texture that holds the filling well.
The combination of egg, meat and cheese provides a complete set of proteins, fats and some B‑vitamins.
Variations with added vegetables (tomato, spinach) make the dish more balanced.
Thermal processing of the meat and egg makes the sandwich safe to digest.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Eggs and meat are complete protein sources essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: B2, B6 and B12 vitamins in the egg and meat support energy metabolism.

items.title: Calcium from cheese
items.content: Cheese adds calcium, important for bones and teeth.

items.title: Energy dense
items.content: Carbohydrates from the bread combined with fats from cheese and meat provide quick and sustained energy.

items.title: Some dietary fiber
items.content: While white bread contains less fiber than whole‑grain varieties, it still contributes a modest amount of dietary fiber.

items.title: High calorie content
items.content: The sandwich can be calorie‑dense due to fats in cheese and meat, so portion control is advisable.

items.title: Saturated fats
items.content: Cheese and certain meats contain saturated fats, which may affect cholesterol levels if consumed in excess.

items.title: Sodium
items.content: Processed meats and cheese often contain high salt, which can be an issue for people with hypertension.

items.title: Allergy to eggs or dairy
items.content: Individuals allergic to eggs or milk products should avoid this sandwich.

content.title: How to Prepare
content.content: Toast the bread until lightly golden. Fry the egg (sunny side up or over hard) and the meat (ham, bacon). On the bottom slice place the meat, then the egg, followed by a slice of cheese. Top with the second slice of bread and let the cheese melt slightly. Optionally add sauce or fresh vegetables.

content.title: Storage
content.content: The sandwich is best eaten fresh. If needed, store in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours, wrapped in food‑grade film. Keep bread and fillings separate when storing to prevent sogginess.

content.title: About
content.content: Puerto Rican Seasoning with Ham (4514) is a flavorful spice blend typical of Puerto Rican cuisine, featuring dried ham, garlic, paprika, oregano, cumin, and aromatic herbs. It delivers a rich, slightly smoky and savory taste, perfect for meat, fish, vegetables, and rice dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The blend is based on traditional Puerto Rican recipes where ham provides the main umami source.
Paprika gives the seasoning its bright red color and a hint of sweetness.
Cumin and oregano add the characteristic Caribbean aroma.
It is commonly used in dishes like arroz con pollo and mofongo.
The dry mix lasts longer than fresh herbs and retains its flavor for years.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: The dried ham component supplies protein important for tissue repair.

items.title: Source of iron
items.content: Ham and spices provide a modest amount of iron, supporting normal blood formation.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Paprika and oregano contain polyphenols that help combat free radicals.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Cumin is known to aid digestive processes and reduce bloating.

items.title: Low in sugar
items.content: The seasoning contains no added sugar, making it suitable for low‑carb diets.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Ham and added salt can increase sodium intake, which may be a concern for hypertension.

items.title: Spice allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be sensitive to paprika, oregano, or cumin.

items.title: Histamine levels
items.content: Dried ham can contain histamines that may trigger reactions in sensitive people.

items.title: Not suitable for vegetarians
items.content: The product contains meat, so vegetarians and vegans should look for plant‑based alternatives.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Sprinkle the seasoning on meat, fish, or poultry before grilling or baking, add it to marinades, soups, rice dishes, and vegetable stews. For a stronger flavor, lightly toast the blend in a dry pan before use.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the seasoning in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. For extended shelf life, keep it in the refrigerator to preserve aroma. Keep moisture out to prevent clumping.

content.title: About
content.content: The whole wheat roll is a soft bun made from whole grain wheat flour. It has a subtle nutty flavor, a dense yet airy texture, and the characteristic aroma of fresh bread. It works well for breakfast, snacks, or as a base for sandwiches.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Whole grain flour retains the bran and germ, making the roll more nutritious than white bread.
Traditionally these rolls were baked across Europe as a staple of daily meals.
Proper dough fermentation preserves natural flavors and improves digestibility.
The roll is often used as a base for open‑face sandwiches with vegetables and lean protein.
Its fiber content helps regulate blood sugar levels.

items.title: Rich in fiber
items.content: Fiber supports digestion, promotes satiety, and maintains a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Whole grain flour provides thiamine, niacin, and folate, which are essential for energy metabolism.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: Compared with white bread, the whole wheat roll raises blood sugar more slowly.

items.title: Source of minerals
items.content: It supplies magnesium, iron, and zinc, important for muscle function and immunity.

items.title: Supports cardiovascular health
items.content: Beneficial fats and antioxidants in whole grains help lower LDL cholesterol.

items.title: Wheat allergy
items.content: People with celiac disease or gluten intolerance should avoid the roll.

items.title: High carbohydrate content
items.content: Those monitoring carb intake should watch portion size.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Some varieties are salted; choose unsalted versions if you have hypertension.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy the whole wheat roll fresh, toasted, or as a sandwich base with lean meat, fish, vegetables, or hummus. It pairs well with low‑fat cheeses and fresh herbs.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the roll in a paper bag or container at room temperature for up to 2‑3 days. For longer storage, freeze in an airtight bag for up to 3 months. Warm in the oven or toaster before serving.

content.title: About
content.content: Sweet tamales are a traditional Mexican dish consisting of a corn‑maize dough (masa) filled with a sweet mixture of fruits, sugar, cinnamon, and sometimes nuts. The dough is made from masa harina, steamed in small parcels, and then wrapped in corn husks or banana leaves before cooking.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Tamales are one of the oldest foods in the Americas, dating back to pre‑Columbian civilizations.
Sweet versions are often served at festivals and Day of the Dead celebrations.
Traditionally the dough is wrapped in corn husks (hojuelas) or banana leaves, which impart a subtle aroma.
Different Mexican regions use various fillings, from pineapple and mango to chocolate and caramel.
Tamales are commonly enjoyed with hot chocolate or spiced coffee.

items.title: Source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: The corn masa provides slow‑releasing energy, helping maintain stable blood‑sugar levels.

items.title: Rich in dietary fiber
items.content: Corn contributes fiber that supports healthy digestion.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The dough contains thiamine, niacin, and folate, important for metabolism.

items.title: Antioxidants in the filling
items.content: Fruits and spices such as cinnamon are rich in antioxidants that combat free radicals.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Tamales provide magnesium and potassium, which aid muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Corn allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to corn‑based products.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Sweet fillings make the dish calorie‑dense; people with diabetes should limit portion size.

items.title: Sodium levels
items.content: If salt is added to the dough, it may be a concern for those with hypertension.

items.title: Food‑borne illness risk
items.content: Tamales must be stored and cooked at proper temperatures to prevent bacterial growth.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Tamales are served hot, unwrapped from their husk. They can be eaten on their own or drizzled with chocolate sauce, caramel, or fruit puree.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cooked tamales in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. For longer storage, freeze them in a freezer‑safe bag; reheat by steaming or microwaving before serving.
